alignments.note: Finite verb with its supplied subject pronoun under rule 9, headed on the lexical verb.
Negative indefinite rendered *nothing*; no separate negator stands in the clause.
Conjunction ὅτι rendered by the second *for*; not recitative, so rule 43 does not arise.
Negative conjunction rendered *neither*; the following τι is rendered non-negatively as *anything*, so rules 41 and 59 leave this negator its own English word (rule 69).
Modal verb rendered *can* with its supplied subject pronoun under rule 9; *can* is the lexical realization of δύναμαι here, not an auxiliary of the infinitive.
Compound infinitive rendered by the phrasal *carry … out*, the particle realizing the ἐκ- prefix; one unit under rule 15, headed on the verb word.
Indefinite rendered non-negatively as *anything*; rule 69 keeps it separate from οὐδέ.

review_notes: οὐδέ keeps *neither* and τι takes a positive *anything*, which is rule 69's case rather than rules 41/59's emptying.
*out* is kept inside ἐξενεγκεῖν's unit as the compound's own particle, not split off.
